findings.finding: All three baseline→improved pairs score domain-knowledge 1→2 as the sparse glossary is replaced with specific SKU/stock/uniqueness/persistence rules. The controlled one-level gain is directionally supported; it does not validate broad accuracy.

Some outputs overclaim capability from configuration or written policy: reliability/consistent environment use, agent environment tool guarantee, targeted verification, maintenance of architecture/domain docs, and structural enforcement. Row-level reasons include exact evidence pointers.
Most unassessed rows are justified by bounded evidence. Two observability=1 ratings are not justified: empty lessons files and CI configuration do not establish actual event records.

Improved domain score is stable at 2,2,2. Healthy domain score varies 3,3,2 despite identical improved/healthy source bytes across matched runs. Repeated ratings vary on several concepts, limiting reproducibility.

controlledPairs.baselineGlossary:
# Domain glossary
Products have SKU and stock fields. Detailed term definitions and business invariants are not documented here yet.
controlledPairs.improvedGlossary:
# Domain glossary
A Product is a catalog entry with a unique nonempty SKU string and a nonnegative integer stock count. SKU means stock keeping unit; it is case-sensitive and is not a display label. A Catalog owns products keyed by SKU. Adding an existing SKU is an error, never an update. Stock is the count of individual available units, not currency or a reservation. Negative and fractional stock are invalid. src/catalog.ts add enforces these invariants and src/catalog.test.ts encodes the duplicate, negative and fractional cases. There is no persistence, order or reservation model.
